## Summary
- cf-0oj5.fu5 — the perf-track follow-on to cf-0klm's ISR unlock.
- Pre-renders every catalog slug at build time + 404s unknown slugs at the edge.
- No runtime Wix SDK roundtrip on PDP requests.
- Closes bd cf-c736.

## Combined effect with prior PRs
- **cf-0klm PR #714 (merged)**: removed cookies() from layout.tsx → ISR eligible
- **cf-0oj5 PR #704 (merged)**: `revalidate=3600` → 1-hr refresh window
- **cf-c736 (this PR)**: `generateStaticParams` + `dynamicParams=false` → build-time pre-render

Result on Vercel: known PDP slugs serve from build cache (instant 200, no Wix roundtrip); unknown slugs return 404 immediately. The revalidate window continues to refresh cached pages every hour for content updates.

## Implementation
- `generateStaticParams()` calls `listAllProducts()` (paginate-to-completion helper from `cfw-upa`; sitemap already uses it). Filters out empty/missing slugs (Wix draft rows can return them; Next.js errors on `slug: undefined`).
- `export const dynamicParams = false` — closed catalog set; non-matching slugs are typos/scrapers, not buyers.

## Build cost
~88 SKU catalog × 1 `listAllProducts` call (100-page size → ~1-2 paginate iterations). Well under the 120s Vercel budget cited in the bead.

## TDD
6 cases (`src/__tests__/ProductsSlugStaticParams.test.ts`):
1. `generateStaticParams` exported as async fn
2. `dynamicParams === false` exported
3. Maps every product to `{ slug }`
4. Filters empty/missing slugs (defensive)
5. Empty `listAllProducts` result tolerated (Wix outage during build)
6. `listAllProducts` called exactly once per build

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run src/__tests__/ProductsSlugStaticParams.test.ts` — 6/6 green
- [x] Co-test with `ProductsSlugPageCaching.test.ts` — 10/10 (revalidate contract preserved)
- [ ] Post-deploy: Vercel preview shows `x-vercel-cache: HIT` on known slug, 404 on unknown
- [ ] Lighthouse re-measurement on kingston-futon-frame — closes cf-0oj5 acceptance

## Iter06 target

`axiom_reduction_note` (`docs/AXIOM_REDUCTION_NOTE.md`).

## Live-state check (rule 1)

Prompt framing: `audited_conditional`, class E missing_bridge_theorem,
356 descendants, repair = supply derivations for D1-D10 reductions.

Live ledger at start of iteration:

- `axiom_reduction_note`: `audit_status: unaudited` (the prior
  `audited_conditional` was invalidated for `criticality_increased:leaf->medium`,
  not a substantive chain failure)
- `effective_status: meta`, `intrinsic_status: meta`, `claim_type: meta`
- `load_bearing_step_class: null` in live row
- `direct_in_degree: 1`, deps = 5 named D-row authority surfaces
- Note self-classifies as inventory-only with `Status authority:
  independent audit lane only` and an explicit "Audit boundary" /
  "Admitted-context derivation gap" section saying it does NOT close
  the D-row derivations

The prompt's repair target (supply in-note derivations) is therefore
**not appropriate**: the note's contract is meta-inventory, not
derivation closure, and the prior auditor's load-bearing class E was
explicitly addressed in the 2026-05-10 audit-narrowing refresh that
predates the criticality bump.

## What this PR does (honest narrow repair)

Refreshes the parenthetical `audit_status: ...` labels for the five
named one-hop authority surfaces in the Audit boundary block. Previously
all five were tagged `(audit_status: unaudited)`; live ledger has moved:

| Dep | Live audit_status | Live intrinsic_status | chain_closes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `born_rule_analysis_2026-04-11` | **`audited_failed`** | `audited_failed` | false |
| `poisson_exhaustive_uniqueness_note` | `unaudited` | `unaudited` | n/a |
| `valley_linear_action_note` | `audited_clean` | `retained_bounded` | true |
| `valley_linear_robustness_note` | `audited_clean` | `retained_bounded` | true |
| `valley_linear_continuum_synthesis_note` | `unaudited` | `unaudited` | n/a |

Edit makes three small changes, all in the meta header / Audit boundary
/ Part 7 framing:

1. Header date stamp adds `2026-05-16 (upstream-state citation refresh)`.
2. The five parenthetical audit-state labels are updated to live values
   (including the `audited_failed` flag on the Born-rule surface and
   the two `audited_clean` flags on valley-linear-action/-robustness),
   and the "Admitted-context derivation gap" summary is rewritten to
   enumerate the mixed state (two clean, two unaudited, one failed)
   rather than asserting uniform absence of closure.
3. A "Current-state caveat (2026-05-16)" is inserted before Part 7
   "Do not say" noting that the Part 7 "Do say" package wording is
   **not** currently warranted because the upstream surfaces are mixed.

## Out of scope (deliberately untouched)

- A1, A2 axioms; C1 dimensional choice
- D1-D10 inventory rows, "Type" / "Description" columns
- Axiom counts ("2 axioms + 1 dimensional choice")
- `claim_type` (remains `meta`); `intrinsic_status`; `effective_status`
- Deps list (same 5 named surfaces)
- All numerical evidence (Part 5)
- All Part 6 open-questions content

No new retained premises. No D-row promoted to in-note closure. No
runner change. No ledger row mutation; canonical pipeline will recompute
`note_hash` on next validation pass.

## Why this is appropriate for the meta-parent

The note's `Authority role` is recorded as "records a meta-inventory of
named in-flight derivation-target rows ... does **not** itself
constitute a derivation closure." The honest repair for a meta-inventory
whose parentheticals have gone stale is to refresh the parentheticals,
not to bolt on derivations the note has explicitly disclaimed.

The user-visible effect: future readers of this note will see the
mixed-state reality (one failed surface, two clean, two pending),
matching the live ledger; the Part 7 publication framing is now gated
on that mixed state rather than on the obsolete "all unaudited" snapshot.

## Re-audit guidance

A re-audit can score against the refreshed parentheticals. If a reviewer
prefers an even narrower repair (drop the Born-rule "Do not say" line,
or move the Current-state caveat earlier), happy to amend; the current
diff prioritizes minimum invasion of the inventory structure.

## Assessment (3 sentences)

Live ledger state differed materially from the prompt's framing:
the prior `audited_conditional` was invalidated for a criticality bump
(not a chain failure), and the note already self-classifies as a meta-
inventory that disclaims D-row closure — exactly what the prompt was
asking it to become. The genuine staleness was in the parenthetical
audit-state citations (all five labeled `unaudited` when one is now
`audited_failed` and two are now `audited_clean`/`retained_bounded`),
so the edit refreshes only that metadata and adds a mixed-state caveat
on Part 7. The note remains a meta-inventory; no new retained premises
or D-row closures were introduced.

## Summary

Adds a two-post series on standing up a multi-tenant Slurm cluster on AWS ParallelCluster, anchored to [`1.architectures/8.accounting-database/`](https://github.com/awslabs/awsome-distributed-ai/tree/main/1.architectures/8.accounting-database) and the prereqs template.

- **Part 1 — Accounting Database + Multi-User Setup** (`content/posts/slurm-accounting-multi-user-on-parallelcluster/`, ~870 lines): provisioning (VPC + FSx prereqs, Aurora Serverless v2 accounting DB, ParallelCluster wired to `SlurmSettings.Database`) and a lightweight no-LDAP multi-user setup (`useradd` on the head node + post-install script propagating UIDs to compute nodes via a CSV on FSx OpenZFS). Ends with the smoke-test demonstrating `slurmdbd` is recording every job with full attribution.
- **Part 2 — QoS Deep Dive** (`content/posts/slurm-qos-on-parallelcluster/`, ~500 lines): associations, QoS limits (`GrpTRES`, `MaxWall`, `MaxJobsPerUser`), multifactor priority + fairshare, preemption, partition QoS, job arrays. Realizes the policy *"research team 50% / interactive 1h+4 GPU cap / batch-lowprio preemptible"* on the cluster Part 1 builds.

Each post cross-links the other. Part 1's wrap-up has a dedicated "Up next — Part 2" section. Part 2 opens with a "Recap — where Part 1 left us" section listing the cluster state Part 1 produces.

Every command in both posts was run on a live cluster (2× `g6.48xlarge` in `us-east-1a`, against a capacity reservation). Outputs (sacct, sshare, squeue, sprio, sacctmgr) are real terminal captures, including:

- preemption demo (charlie's `batch-lowprio` 16-GPU job requeued by alice's `research` job)
- the GrpTRES cap rejecting `sbatch --gres=gpu:5` against `interactive` with ExitCode `0:53`

body:
## Hypothesis

The current model uses `mlp_ratio=2`, meaning the FFN intermediate dimension is `2 × n_hidden = 256`. Halving to `mlp_ratio=1` (FFN dim = 128 = n_hidden) cuts **~25% of per-step matmul cost** — potentially gaining 4-6 extra epochs in the 30-min wall-clock budget.

Context: we identified that per-batch FFN overhead dominates compute in this architecture (slice_num=8 only saved 5% wall-clock despite eliminating 75% of slice-attention pairs; the FFN matmuls are the bottleneck). edward's PR #3769 attacks this by dropping a whole Transolver block (n_layers=5→4). This PR attacks it from the other direction: keeping all 5 blocks but halving the FFN width.

**Why it might win:** In the compute-bound regime, +4-6 epochs ≈ +8-12pt val improvement based on the per-epoch trajectory trend. If the capacity loss from a smaller FFN is less than the compute gain from more epochs, this wins.

**Why it might lose:** The FFN in Transolver encodes the per-node MLP transform after slice attention. If n_hidden=128 FFN with ratio=1 (128-dim hidden layer) loses too much representational capacity relative to the current 256-dim, accuracy drops.

**Orthogonal to edward's work:** edward drops a block (less depth), this halves width (less width). If both win, they compound. If one wins, we learn which FFN dimension matters more.

## Instructions

In `target/train.py`, find the `mlp_ratio` parameter in the model config dict (search for `mlp_ratio`) and change it from `2` to `1`:

```python
# Before
mlp_ratio=2,

# After
mlp_ratio=1,
```

No other changes. Run a single seed:

```bash
cd target/
python train.py --experiment_name mlp-ratio-1 --agent charliepai2i48h1-alphonse
```

**Key diagnostics to include in your results:**
1. `sec/epoch` and total epochs completed in the 30-min cap — this is the CRITICAL diagnostic
2. Full per-split val and test MAE
3. Per-epoch val_avg trajectory (first 5 and last 5 epochs)

**Note on model size:** mlp_ratio=1 reduces the FFN intermediate from 256 to 128 dims. The per-head attention remains unchanged (n_head=4, n_hidden=128). Peak GPU memory should drop; sec/epoch should drop proportionally to the FFN savings.

## Baseline

Current best (PR #3950, **slice_num=12**, EMA=0.997, n_head=4, **mlp_ratio=2**, epoch 18):

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `val_avg/mae_surf_p` **(beat this)** | **80.60** |
| `test_avg/mae_surf_p` | **71.14** |
| `val_single_in_dist` | 93.82 |
| `val_geom_camber_rc` | 93.06 |
| `val_geom_camber_cruise` | 60.47 |
| `val_re_rand` | 75.05 |
| sec/epoch | ~103s |
| epochs in 30-min cap | 18 |

Single-seed variance ±5-10 pts. A clean win here would be -3%+ (driven by compute savings).

**Reproduce baseline:**
```bash
cd target/
python train.py --experiment_name mlp-ratio-2-baseline-repro --agent charliepai2i48h1-alphonse
```

author: bryanpsd
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `Content-Security-Policy` response header to `netlify.toml` for all routes (`/*`)
- Explicitly allowlists every external resource host the site legitimately uses
- Locks down `object-src`, `base-uri`, and `form-action` to prevent plugin injection, `<base>` tag hijacking, and cross-origin form submissions
- Adds `upgrade-insecure-requests` to force HTTP → HTTPS

## What's allowed and why

| Directive | Hosts | Reason |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| `script-src` | self + GTM, GA, google.com, maps.googleapis.com, gstatic.com | GA4 loader, reCAPTCHA, Google Maps JS API |
| `style-src` | self + fonts.googleapis.com | Google Fonts stylesheet |
| `font-src` | self + fonts.gstatic.com | Google Fonts files |
| `img-src` | self + images.ctfassets.net, maps.googleapis/gstatic.com, GA | Contentful images, Maps tiles, GA pixel |
| `connect-src` | self + GA, analytics.google.com, googleapis.com, cdn.contentful.com | Fetch/XHR targets |
| `frame-src` | google.com, recaptcha.google.com | reCAPTCHA v3 challenge iframes |
| `worker-src` | self + blob: | `/sw.js` service worker |

## Note on `'unsafe-inline'`

`'unsafe-inline'` is present on `script-src` and `style-src`. This is unavoidable because Astro's `is:inline` directive and the Google Analytics init script produce inline JS in the HTML at build time. Netlify's static headers make nonces infeasible. The real XSS protection here comes from the strict external-host allowlist — a script injected via XSS cannot load from an arbitrary domain.

- [ ] Deploy to a Netlify preview and verify the `Content-Security-Policy` header is present in response headers
- [ ] Open browser DevTools → Console: confirm no CSP violations on the home page, contact page, and a course page (which loads Google Maps)

body:
This patch addresses a **critical integer overflow vulnerability** in the Jassimp JNI bindings that could lead to heap buffer overflow. The fix implements overflow-safe arithmetic helpers and replaces manual memory management with RAII-based `std::vector` containers.

## Vulnerability Details

### Issue
- **Type:** Integer overflow in buffer size computation
- **Component:** Jassimp JNI (Java Native Interface bindings for Assimp)
- **Affected Code:** Face buffer sizing in `loadMeshes()` function
- **Attack Vector:** Malformed 3D model files with excessive face counts or vertex indices
- **Impact:** Heap buffer overflow → memory corruption, DoS, potential code execution

### Root Cause
When computing face buffer sizes, the code performed unchecked multiplication:
```cpp
// VULNERABLE: No overflow check
size_t faceBufferSize = mesh->mNumFaces * 3 * sizeof(int);
```

If `mNumFaces` is large enough, `mNumFaces * 3` overflows `size_t`, resulting in a smaller allocation than needed. Subsequent writes overflow the heap buffer.

## Solution Overview

### 1. **Overflow-Safe Arithmetic Library** (`jassimp_overflow.h`)
New header-only library providing:

- **`safeMultiplySize(a, b, result)`** — Multiplies two `size_t` values; returns `false` if overflow detected
- **`safeAddSize(a, b, result)`** — Adds two `size_t` values; returns `false` if overflow detected  
- **`fitsInJavaInt(value)`** — Validates that a `size_t` fits within Java's signed 32-bit int (`INT_MAX = 2,147,483,647`)
- **`computeFaceBufferSize(mesh, result)`** — Combined helper for safe face buffer sizing with Java int boundary check

### 2. **RAII-Based Buffer Management** (`jassimp.cpp`)
Replaced all `malloc()` / `free()` patterns with `std::vector<char>`:

**Before:**
```cpp
unsigned int* faceBuffer = (unsigned int*)malloc(faceBufferSize);
// ... use buffer ...
free(faceBuffer);
```

**After:**
```cpp
std::vector<char> faceBuffer(faceBufferSize);
// ... use faceBuffer.data() ...
// Automatic cleanup via RAII destructor
```

**Benefits:**
- Automatic memory cleanup (no leaks)
- Exception safety (no manual free on early return)
- Stack trace clarity (vector vs. bare pointer)

## Security Implications

### Before Patch
-  Integer overflow possible with `mNumFaces > SIZE_MAX / 3`
-  No Java int boundary checks
-  Manual memory management (leak/double-free risks)
-  Undefined behavior on malformed models

### After Patch
-  All arithmetic overflow paths validated
-  Java int boundaries enforced (INT_MAX check)
-  RAII cleanup (automatic, exception-safe)
-  Graceful rejection of malformed models
-  Comprehensive regression test coverage


## Code Quality Improvements

1. **Safety:** RAII patterns eliminate manual memory bugs
2. **Clarity:** Explicit overflow checks document assumptions
3. **Testability:** JNI-free helpers enable unit testing
4. **Maintainability:** Clear ownership semantics (vector vs. pointer)
5. **Portability:** Standard C++ (no platform-specific assumptions)

body:
Three operator-facing bugs found testing 0.7.0 against a real dhis2-themed daemon + a Playwright screenshot capture pass.

## Bugs fixed

1. **Theme race on first sign-in**: the login modal's pre-paint `applyModalTheme()` wrote CSS variables to `:root` and competed with the artifact's `applyTheme()`. `--header-bg` was left unset, so the DHIS2 blue header bar didn't appear until a manual reload. **Fix**: the modal renders with literal inline colours; no `:root` writes. The artifact owns theme variables end-to-end.

2. **5-second delay on sign-in**: `_auth.js` wrapped `CK_AUTH.on()` to record subscribers in its own dict and called `_emit('token-set')` from sign-in. But `_state.js`'s `useLiveState` registered `pull` via the closure-captured original `on` (before any wrapper could intercept), so `_emit` reached nothing — the dashboard waited for the next polling tick. **Fix**: `_state.js` exposes `emit` directly; `_auth.js` calls `CK_AUTH.emit('token-set')`. Refetch fires in the next render cycle.

3. **Sign-out hidden in the palette**: operators didn't know they could sign out without opening Ctrl+K. **Fix**: "sign out" button in the top-right header (visible when a token is stored). Replaces the previous "reload config" pill — reload is still accessible via the palette.

## UX additions

- **Theme-aware modal palette**: each theme has its own `titleInk` / `inputBorder` / `btnBg` / `btnInk` / `btnBorder`. dhis2 specifically uses `#1f4d75` (the header blue) for the title + Sign in button.
- **`tui --connect URL` interactive token prompt**: probes `/api/auth`, prompts for the token on TTY when not provided via `--token` / `--token-env` (hidden input, same UX as `verify --url --token`).
- **`tui` local-mode heads-up**: prints a one-line note when `[auth]` is configured explaining that `[auth]` only gates `chap-checker serve` — local TUI has no HTTP and doesn't need a token.

## Screenshots

- All browser screenshots regenerated against an auth-enabled deployment (sign-out button visible in top-right).
- New `web-dashboard-login{,-dhis2}.png` captures of the login modal in both themes.
- TUI screenshots regenerated.

body:
## Summary

This PR removes the complex CRX3 signing and auto-update infrastructure, pivoting to a simpler manual sideload distribution model. It also introduces security controls to restrict image fetching and export to approved domains, with a new Settings page for users to customize these restrictions.

## Key Changes

- **Removed auto-update pipeline**: Deleted CRX3 signing logic, RSA key generation, protobuf encoding, and GitHub Pages release artifacts (`docs/update.xml`, `docs/meta.json`, `install.ps1`). The extension is now distributed as a simple ZIP for manual installation only.

- **Simplified build script**: `build.ps1` now only packages extension files into a ZIP, removing 167 lines of cryptographic and release infrastructure. Dropped PowerShell 7 requirement (now works with PS 5+).

- **Added security framework** (`security.js`):
  - Centralized security defaults: approved image hosts (Microsoft 365 services) and approved tab domains
  - URL validation helpers (`isApprovedUrl`, `secMatchesHost`) with wildcard pattern support (e.g., `*.sharepoint.com`)
  - Deliberately excludes `*.sharepoint.com` wildcard to prevent credentialed fetches to arbitrary tenants

- **New Settings page** (`options.html`, `options.js`):
  - Users can customize approved image servers and extension domains
  - One hostname per line with wildcard support
  - Settings persist via `chrome.storage.sync`

- **Enhanced background service worker** (`background.js`):
  - Seeds storage with security defaults on install/update
  - Validates download requests (MIME type, filename safety)
  - Authenticates message senders (only own extension pages)
  - Validates image fetch URLs against approved hosts before fetching

- **Content security in extractor** (`extractor.js`):
  - Added `sanitizeHref()` to block `javascript:`, `data:`, and other unsafe schemes
  - Added `sanitizeHtml()` to strip dangerous tags (script, iframe, form, svg) and event handlers
  - Applied sanitization to all citation links and rich HTML content

- **Export validation** (`popup.js`):
  - Checks active tab URL against approved domains before export
  - Reports blocked images in export status with count and guidance to update Settings
  - Loads security module for URL validation

- **Improved print isolation** (`print.js`, `print.html`):
  - Added `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` to iframe to prevent injected scripts from running in extension context
  - Moved print trigger to parent frame to keep all JS out of sandboxed iframe

- **Updated documentation** (`docs/index.html`, `README.md`):
  - Removed PowerShell one-liner install method
  - Emphasized manual sideload as the only supported installation method
  - Updated privacy statement to mention domain and server approval controls

## Notable Implementation Details

- Security defaults are intentionally conservative: only Microsoft-owned domains are pre-approved for image fetching
- SharePoint image fetching requires explicit user configuration (per-tenant) to prevent supply-chain risk
- All URL validation happens in the service worker before any network request
- Sender authentication in background.js prevents content scripts or external pages from triggering downloads
- HTML sanitization uses DOMParser to safely strip dangerous content while preserving formatting

Pull Request: Приведение эндпоинта создания товара в соответствие с OpenAPI Spec (US-B2B-01)
Описание
Это повторная сдача квеста по реализации эндпоинта POST /api/v1/products. В текущей итерации код был полностью синхронизирован с актуальной спецификацией openapi.yaml и требованиями "canonic flow".

Что изменилось:
Модель Product: Добавлены обязательные поля slug, blocking_reason_id и moderator_comment. Поле blocked удалено, так как статус теперь управляется через status и причины блокировки.
Схемы API:
ProductCreate: добавлена валидация обязательного наличия хотя бы одного изображения, планируется PR в общую спецификацию (DoD requirement).
ProductResponse: добавлены все недостающие поля из спецификации.
Важно: Поле category оставлено во вложенном виде (CategoryRef) вместо плоского category_id. Это осознанное отклонение от текущей схемы openapi.yaml для сохранения удобства фронтенда, планируется PR в общую спецификацию(НО сейчас оставлены оба поля, category_id отдельным полем для соответствия контракту).
Бизнес-логика: Добавлена автоматическая генерация slug из title при создании товара.
Инфраструктура: Настроен пайплайн GitHub Actions для автоматического запуска тестов в контейнеризированном окружении (Postgres + MinIO).
ADR: Способ хранения характеристик товара
Контекст: Необходимо выбрать структуру хранения динамических характеристик (напр. "Бренд", "Материал"). Рассмотренные варианты:

EAV-схема (Entity-Attribute-Value).
Отдельная таблица CharacteristicValue.
JSON-поле (JSONB) в таблице Product (Выбрано).
Критерии выбора:

Сложность запросов: JSONB позволяет выполнять фильтрацию встроенными средствами PostgreSQL без множественных JOIN-ов.
Удобство разработки: Pydantic бесшовно валидирует структуру JSON, что упрощает код сервисного слоя и ускоряет разработку на начальном этапе.
Definition of Done (DoD)
Соответствие user-flow: Пройден сценарий «создание товара» из b2b-flows.md.
Тесты (13+ passed):
create_product_returns_201_with_created_status: товар создаётся со статусом CREATED.
seller_id_taken_from_jwt: ID продавца берется строго из JWT, защита от IDOR реализована.
missing_images_returns_400: валидация на отсутствие картинок работает.
missing_category_returns_400 / invalid_category_id_returns_400: валидация категорий реализована.
OpenAPI: Схемы запросов и ответов (за исключением вложенности категории) соответствуют openapi.yaml.
GitHub Actions: Пайплайн настроен и проходит успешно.

author: brentmitchell25
body:
Closes #9652

## Summary

Before this PR, OAuth resource handling centered on `validAudiences`: a flat list of acceptable audience/resource identifiers. That can validate whether a requested `resource` is known, but it cannot express resource-server policy or per-client entitlement. This PR replaces that with explicit protected-resource rows and uses the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter as the contract boundary.

## Architectural approach

- Persist protected resources as `oauthResource` rows, with `oauthClientResource` links for per-client entitlement. `enforcePerClientResources` makes the entitlement check part of authorization, token issuance, and Dynamic Client Registration instead of a caller-side convention.
- Resolve token policy from the requested resources: most-restrictive TTL wins, scopes are narrowed by resource allowlists, per-resource custom claims are merged after stripping RFC 9068 reserved claim names, and JWT access tokens include `jti`.
- Keep signing policy close to the resource being protected. A resource can pin `signingAlgorithm` or `signingKeyId`; the JWT plugin adds the key lookup and multi-algorithm keyring support needed to honor that without special casing OAuth issuance.
- Move protected-resource metadata responsibility to the resource-server side. The OAuth provider exposes resource CRUD/linking plus challenge helpers; `@better-auth/mcp` now declares an explicit `resource`, persists it, publishes RFC 9728 metadata for that MCP resource, and binds issued access tokens to it.
- Route all resource validation through the same source of truth. Config seeding, admin CRUD, DCR, authorize, token, introspection, revocation, and userinfo all resolve against `oauthResource` rather than rebuilding partial allowlist checks in each endpoint.

## Reviewer notes

- This is a breaking OAuth provider change: `validAudiences` is removed in favor of `resources` / `oauthResource`, and the MCP plugin now requires an explicit `resource` option.
- DCR `resources` are validated through the lazy seed path and linked to the new client transactionally, so self-registered clients cannot bypass configured resource policy or observe half-created state.
- Admin resource creation relies on the database uniqueness boundary instead of a read-before-write check, avoiding the previous race window.
- This PR does not implement DPoP/mTLS proof validation, JWE access tokens, or per-resource opaque-token format. Those remain out of scope for this diff.

## Related

- RFC 8707, RFC 9068, RFC 9728, RFC 7591 §2

author: getvictor
body:
The agent half of the issue #11 process-baseline-enumeration work. The server half landed in PR #42 (4ccf594): exec payloads accept an optional `snapshot` bool, the detection engine drops `snapshot=true` exec events from rule evaluation, and the graph builder absorbs them via insertExecWithoutFork.

This commit adds the extension-side enumeration that produces those events. Without it, anything already running when the ES extension activates (Safari, Slack, Finder, every long-lived system daemon) stays invisible in the process tree forever.

What this changes:

* ProcessSnapshotEnumerator.swift (new) walks the live process table via sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_ALL) and emits a synthetic exec event per live PID with snapshot=true. The kinfo_proc reply carries pid/ppid/uid/gid, so we get the parent linkage and credentials in one syscall; proc_pidpath resolves the executable path per PID. args, cwd, code_signing, sha256 are left empty for the baseline.

  sysctl rather than proc_listallpids: on macOS 26, proc_listallpids is heavily filtered even for root callers. Empirical QA on the SIP-disabled dev VM showed 56 of 473 live PIDs returned (12%), with PID 1 and all low-PID daemons absent. KERN_PROC_ALL is what ps uses and surfaces every process the caller has permission to see, which for a root-level ES extension is the full table.

* EventSerializer.swift grows an optional `snapshot` field on ExecPayload with a custom encode(to:) that omits the key when false. Live exec events therefore stay byte-identical to the pre-snapshot wire shape; only baseline events carry the field.

* XPCServer.swift gains waitForFirstPeer(timeout:). The snapshot enumerator emits 400+ events in ~20 ms, which would otherwise be delivered into an empty peer set during the post-restart XPC reconnect window and silently lost. The barrier is a one-shot semaphore signaled by the first listener-accepted peer; subsequent connects/disconnects do not retrigger it.

* main.swift schedules the snapshot pass onto a utility-qos background queue after subscriber.start(), gated on waitForFirstPeer. Running after subscribe (not before) means processes that exec between enumeration and subscribe are caught by the live stream; the small race the other way (a snapshot row for a PID whose exit just landed live) is handled gracefully by the graph builder's existing UpdateProcessExit + insertExecWithoutFork flow.

QA on the edr-dev VM (host_id 93DFC6F5-...):

Active process count went from 27 to 365 after the snapshot pass. Low-PID daemon count (pid < 500) went from 0 to 122. PID 1 launchd, PID 128 syslogd, PID 251 nsurlsessiond, PID 561
ContinuityCaptureAgent, PID 683 Spotlight, PID 911 distnoted etc. all visible in the process tree. No new detection alerts fired post-restart, confirming the engine filter is dropping snapshot=true events before rule evaluation. SigNoz traces show clean /api/events 200 responses with no ingest errors.

Known follow-up (#173): snapshot-derived rows still get force-exited by the 6h TTL reconciler from issue #6. Tracked separately as a combined is_snapshot column + agent heartbeat for liveness pings.

Build, swiftlint (zero violations on the four touched files), and the existing server detection/engine test suite all pass.

author: niklas-joh
body:
## Summary

Closes #569. Four bugs found through deep root-cause analysis, all fixed in one PR.

### Bug 1 — Critical: PHP fatal error on Generator page

`GeneratorModule` was calling `new ProviderFactory()` with **no arguments**, but `ProviderFactory::__construct()` requires a mandatory `ProviderSettings` argument. PHP 8.x throws `ArgumentCountError` (an `Error`, not `Exception`), which bypassed the existing `catch (\Exception $e)` block entirely and crashed PHP — producing "There has been a critical error on this website."

Every other module (Seo, Images, Chat, ChatPage) correctly passes `new ProviderSettings()` to the constructor. Generator was the sole outlier.

### Bug 2 — Wrong model selection in Generator

`$provider->get_models()[0]['id']` accessed integer key `0` on a **string-keyed** associative array, always yielding `null` and ultimately passing an empty model string to the provider. Replaced with `$provider->get_default_model()`.

### Bug 3 — Usage double-counting in Generator and SEO (compounding issue #568)

Both handlers called `NJ_Usage_Tracker::log_usage()` after `provider->complete()`, but the **provider layer already logs exactly once** (proxy for trial/pro_managed via `NJ_Proxy_Client::chat()`; `AbstractProvider::maybe_log()` for pro_byok). The handler-level calls double-counted all tokens for all tiers. Removed both redundant calls. `ChatRestController` was the correct reference pattern all along: it never calls `log_usage()` directly.

This means the dashboard was showing **2× the actual token spend** — which also made issue #568 appear even worse than it really was.

### Bug 4 — Defensive: `catch (\Exception)` misses PHP Errors

Broadened `catch (\Exception $e)` to `catch (\Throwable $e)` in both `GeneratorModule` and `SeoModule`. `TypeError`, `ArgumentCountError`, and other `Error` subclasses are not caught by `catch (\Exception)` — this is what allowed Bug 1 to escape as a fatal instead of returning a clean 500 JSON response.

### SEO error message surfacing

The specific provider error message (e.g. "Proxy authentication failed. Please reload and try again.") was previously swallowed and replaced with a generic string. Now it is preserved so users see actionable guidance when the proxy token is stale or the site is not registered.

---

## Why tests didn't catch Bug 1

- **`GeneratorTierGatingTest`** only exercises the `permission_callback` in isolation via Brain Monkey — it never calls `handle_generate()`.
- **`TierFeatureMatrixTest::trial/generator`** dispatches a real REST request that *would* expose the crash — but integration tests run under `phpunit-integration.xml.dist` (requires `WP_TESTS_DIR`) and **are not executed in CI**. Only `tests/Unit/` runs automatically.
- **E2E Playwright tests** mock the REST endpoint at the network layer — PHP never executes.

---

## Test plan

- [x] All 309 existing unit tests pass (`./vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Unit/`)
- [x] New `GeneratorModuleTest` added covering: 403 for subscriber, 403 for free tier, 201 happy path with draft post created in DB, prompt injection (title + keywords in outbound request), 500 on provider failure
- [ ] Run integration suite locally: `./vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit-integration.xml.dist tests/Integration/Generator/`
- [ ] On local Docker: reproduce original fatal → apply fix → confirm 201 with draft post
- [ ] Verify dashboard token count is no longer doubled after the double-logging fix
- [ ] For the SEO 502: load any WP admin page to trigger `admin_init → maybe_register()` re-registration of the site token, then retry SEO generate

🚨 Wrangler affected by OS Command Injection in `wrangler pages deploy`

Summary

A command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) has been found to exist in the wrangler pages deploy command. The issue occurs because the --commit-hash parameter is passed directly to a shell command without proper validation or sanitization, allowing an attacker with control of --commit-hash to execute arbitrary commands on the system running Wrangler.

Root cause

The commitHash variable, derived from user input via the --commit-hash CLI argument, is interpolated directly into a shell command using template literals (e.g., execSync(`git show -s --format=%B ${commitHash}`)). Shell metacharacters are interpreted by the shell, enabling command execution.

Impact

This vulnerability is generally hard to exploit, as it requires --commit-hash to be attacker controlled. The vulnerability primarily affects CI/CD environments where wrangler pages deploy is used in automated pipelines and the --commit-hash parameter is populated from external, potentially untrusted sources. An attacker could exploit this to:

  • Run any shell command.
  • Exfiltrate environment variables.
  • Compromise the CI runner to install backdoors or modify build artifacts.

body:
## Hypothesis (H14 — Asymmetric Learning Rate for Surface Output Head)

The Wave 30 fleet has now closed **6 model-side / architecture-layer attacks** (H1 cylindrical, H2 spectral, H3 soft-routing, H4 hard-routing, H5 Y-arch, H7 normal-aux). The architecture-layer attack surface is **DEFINITIVELY exhausted** for the τ_z structural bottleneck — all 6 closures show the same engaged-but-neutral signature (val widening 1.50–1.55 → test collapse to 1.44–1.47 baseline band).

H6 (tanjiro #1134) broke that pattern via hard τ·n=0 projection → test τz/τx=1.281 (mechanism PASS, absolute FAIL): definitive proof that **the bottleneck is at the output-head layer**, but hard projection throws away ~5-8% of real GT normal-component signal.

The current Wave 30 in-flight fleet covers:
- **Loss layer (3-strong)**: H6' soft τ·n penalty (#1147), H12 magnitude-weighted MSE (#1151), H13 tangent/normal anisotropic (#1152)
- **Data-input layer (3-strong)**: H8 mirror-symmetry aug (#1143), H9' curvature input feature (#1146), H11 multi-scale kNN context (#1150)
- **Output-head layer (1-strong)**: H10 vector-decoupled head (#1148)
- **Optimization layer (0-strong)**: ← THIS IS THE COMPLETELY UNDER-ATTACKED SURFACE

**H14 fills the optimization-layer gap**: split optimizer parameter groups so the `surface_out.*` MLP receives a **5× higher learning rate** than the backbone. Two motivations:

1. **The H6 mechanism PASS confirmed the output head IS the bottleneck location**. Pushing more gradient signal into those specific parameters is the most direct attack consistent with that diagnostic.
2. **Standard Kaggle / ImageNet precedent**: classifier heads consistently benefit from higher LR than feature backbones during fine-tuning (e.g., DeiT/timm `head_init_scale`, MAE linear probing protocol, ULMFit slanted triangular). The intuition: the output projection sees a fixed feature distribution and needs to rapidly adapt to the task, while the backbone needs gentler updates to preserve geometry-aware structure.

**Mechanism if H14 wins**:
- `surface_out` parameters update with effective LR ~2.5e-3 (5× the 5e-4 base) under cosine schedule
- The 2-layer surface MLP (n_hidden=512 → 512 → 4) has ~263k params, ~0.5% of total
- Heightened LR on these 263k params drives faster adaptation of the τ-direction-and-magnitude projection without disturbing the slice-attention representation
- If test τz/τx drops below baseline 1.45 (without floor breach), it confirms output-head capacity-budget was the real constraint

**Mechanism if H14 loses (likely outcomes)**:
- Same engaged-but-neutral signature → output-head LR budget is NOT the issue; problem is upstream (the backbone representation doesn't encode τ_z well enough at any output projection)
- Training instability (NaN, divergence) → asymmetric LR ratio too aggressive; falsifies the simple "more LR on head" hypothesis but motivates a follow-up sweep at 2-3x

## Instructions

**File to modify:** `target/train.py`, specifically `build_optimizer` at line 246 onward.

### Implementation outline

Add a new Config field near `lr`:

```python
@dataclass
class Config:
    ...
    lr: float = 5e-4
    weight_decay: float = 5e-4
    # H14 asymmetric LR for surface output head
    surface_out_lr_multiplier: float = 1.0  # 1.0 = baseline; 5.0 = H14 active arm
```

Modify `build_optimizer` to split parameters into two groups:

```python
def build_optimizer(model: nn.Module, config: Config) -> torch.optim.Optimizer:
    optimizer_name = config.optimizer.lower()

    # Split named_parameters into surface_out head vs. everything else.
    head_params = []
    backbone_params = []
    for name, p in model.named_parameters():
        if not p.requires_grad:
            continue
        # Match `surface_out.*` regardless of DDP wrapping (module.surface_out.* or surface_out.*)
        if "surface_out" in name.split("."):
            head_params.append(p)
        else:
            backbone_params.append(p)

    base_lr = config.lr
    head_lr = base_lr * float(config.surface_out_lr_multiplier)

    # Log split for sanity
    backbone_count = sum(p.numel() for p in backbone_params)
    head_count = sum(p.numel() for p in head_params)
    print(
        f"[build_optimizer] backbone params: {backbone_count:,} @ lr={base_lr:.2e}; "
        f"head (surface_out): {head_count:,} @ lr={head_lr:.2e} "
        f"(multiplier={config.surface_out_lr_multiplier:.2f})"
    )

    param_groups = [
        {"params": backbone_params, "lr": base_lr, "name": "backbone"},
        {"params": head_params,     "lr": head_lr,  "name": "surface_out_head"},
    ]

    if optimizer_name == "adamw":
        return torch.optim.AdamW(param_groups, weight_decay=config.weight_decay)
    if optimizer_name == "lion":
        from lion_pytorch import Lion
        return Lion(
            param_groups,
            weight_decay=config.weight_decay,
            betas=(config.lion_beta1, config.lion_beta2),
            use_triton=False,
        )
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown optimizer '{config.optimizer}'. Supported: adamw, lion.")
```

### LR scheduler compatibility check

The cosine LR scheduler (`get_lr_scheduler` or similar — find it in `trainer_runtime.py` or the main training loop near `scheduler = ...`) typically scales each param_group's LR by the same cosine factor. PyTorch's `CosineAnnealingLR` and friends preserve per-group ratios automatically: at any step, `group['lr'] = group['initial_lr'] * cosine_factor`. **Verify** that the scheduler in use does this. If a custom scheduler is hard-coded to a single `lr` value, modify it to iterate per-group.

Specifically check `target/trainer_runtime.py` for the LR schedule implementation and confirm both param groups will be scaled. If they're not, you'll need to add per-group scaling.

### Log per-group LR to W&B every epoch

Add to the W&B `log_metrics` dict in the train loop:
```python
metrics["lr/backbone"] = optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"]
metrics["lr/surface_out_head"] = optimizer.param_groups[1]["lr"]
metrics["lr/head_to_backbone_ratio"] = (
    optimizer.param_groups[1]["lr"] / max(optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"], 1e-12)
)
```

Should hold steady at 5.0 throughout training (modulo cosine scaling).

### Sanity-check: matching baseline at multiplier=1.0

Before launching the H14 arm at 5×, **run a 1-epoch viability check at multiplier=1.0** to confirm:
- The split optimizer produces bit-identical (or near-identical, within numerical noise) results vs the original `model.parameters()` path
- Both param groups have nonzero param counts
- The W&B `lr/head_to_backbone_ratio` logs as exactly 1.0
- No NaN in either group's gradients

This protects against subtle bugs (e.g., missing some params via the `"surface_out" in name.split(".")` rule).

### Reproduce command (H14 active arm, multiplier=5.0)

```bash
cd target/
torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 train.py \
  --batch-size 4 \
  --epochs 13 \
  --lr 5e-4 \
  --lr-warmup-epochs 1 \
  --optimizer lion \
  --weight-decay 5e-4 \
  --data-root /mnt/new-pvc/Processed/drivaerml_processed_rawcanon_20260511 \
  --manifest data/split_manifest.json \
  --train-surface-points 40000 \
  --eval-surface-points 65536 \
  --train-volume-points 49152 \
  --eval-volume-points 65536 \
  --tau-z-loss-weight 2.0 \
  --surface-loss-weight 2.0 \
  --model-layers 5 \
  --model-hidden-dim 512 \
  --model-heads 4 \
  --model-slices 128 \
  --use-qk-norm \
  --surface-out-lr-multiplier 5.0 \
  --wandb-group wave30_asymmetric_lr_h14 \
  --wandb-name alphonse/h14-headlr5x-rank{rank}
```

(If your CLI parser auto-generates `--surface-out-lr-multiplier` from the dataclass via reflection — and it does at line ~233-241 of `train.py` — no extra parse_args change is needed.)

### Expected EP gate guidance

- **EP1 sanity**: val_abupt ≤ 33% (warmup floor); `lr/head_to_backbone_ratio = 5.0` confirmed in W&B logs
- **EP3 PASS**: val_abupt ≤ 6.5%
- **EP6 PASS**: val_abupt ≤ 6.3%
- **EP10 PASS**: val_abupt ≤ 6.15%
- **EP13 terminal**: full

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #5209. This extends `KUBO_TRANSPORT` to lower-dimensional Gamma-supercell calculations by making the transport normalization depend on the CP2K cell periodicity.

For 3D periodic cells, and for the existing isolated finite-box smoke-test path with `PERIODIC NONE`, the previous 3D conductivity output is preserved. For lower-dimensional cells, the displacement operator is projected onto the periodic subspace before the Kubo tensor is evaluated:

- `PERIODIC XY`, `XZ`, or `YZ`: transport is normalized by the periodic area and reported as a 2D sheet conductivity in `S`; carrier densities are reported in `m^-2`.
- `PERIODIC X`, `Y`, or `Z`: transport is normalized by the periodic length and reported as a 1D transport coefficient in `S*m`; carrier densities are reported in `m^-1`.

The projection is built from the actual periodic cell vectors, so it is not limited to orthorhombic slabs/ribbons. This avoids artificial dependence on vacuum height/width for monolayers and quasi-1D nanoribbons, including one-layer-thick systems.

## Implementation details

- Adds a periodic-subspace projection matrix to the Kubo commutator kernel.
- Adds dimensional normalization by periodic length/area/volume.
- Keeps the full Cartesian 3x3 tensor output, but reports dimension-appropriate scalar/tensor units.
- Keeps the old `sigma_iso[S/cm]` matcher output for 3D, and adds separate matcher lines for 2D and 1D.
- Updates the input-section description to document the 1D/2D normalization behavior.

## Tests

Adds two GPW+OT H2 smoke/regression cases under `QS/regtest-kubo-transport`:

- `H2-kubo-2d.inp`: `PERIODIC XY`, exercising sheet-conductivity output in `S`.
- `H2-kubo-1d.inp`: `PERIODIC X`, exercising 1D output in `S*m`.

| File | New tests | Poshi rows |

| `test/components/fixtures/productFixtures.js` | — | (Block 0.2 fixture module) |
| `test/components/AddToCart/AddToCart.spec.tsx` | 5 | `AssertViewAllVariantsButtonRedirectsToProductDetailsPage`, `CanAddToCart{SingleSkuDynamic,SingleSkuStatic}PriceBundledProductFromProductCard`, `CannotAddToCart{MultipleSkuDynamic,MultipleSkuStatic}PriceBundledProductFromProductCard` |

### Mapping notes

The storefront product-card "view all variants vs quantity+add" decision lives at the catalog-layout level, not in the `AddToCart` React component. The component receives a single resolved `cpInstance`, so the Poshi distinctions translate to `cpInstance` flags:

| Poshi semantic | `cpInstance` shape | AddToCart behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Single-SKU bundled product | `purchasable: true` | button enabled |
| Multi-SKU bundled product | `purchasable: false` | button disabled (surrounding card surfaces a "view all variants" link) |

`AssertViewAllVariantsButtonRedirectsToProductDetailsPage` asserts the redirect happens upstream of `AddToCart`; the Unit-equivalent here is the disabled-button state that lets the card render the variants link.

Doc-comments in `productFixtures.js` record this mapping so a future reader doesn't have to re-derive it. STATUS at `~/Projects/Liferay/tests/conversions/STATUS-2026-05-16-block-2.2.md`.

## O que muda

Sprint 6.0 PR 2 — implementa [ADR-024](https://github.com/FabioCaffarello/brasil-a-vera/blob/main/docs/architecture/ADR/024-acentos-secundarios-accent-roxo.md). Adiciona a camada de acento narrativo (`--accent` roxo) + 3 utilitários CSS que o protótipo do designer parceiro estabeleceu, **sem regredir WCAG AA, sem duplicar tokens existentes, sem inflacionar bundle**.

### Tokens novos

| Token | Light (OKLCH) | Dark (OKLCH) |
|---|---|---|
| `--accent` | `0.45 0.18 295` (roxo escurecido) | `0.62 0.22 295` (roxo brilhante) |
| `--accent-foreground` | `1 0 0` (branco) | `0.14 0.012 260` (= `--background`) |

Mapeados via `@theme inline` como `--color-accent` / `--color-accent-foreground`. Consumíveis como `bg-accent`, `text-accent`, etc.

### Utilitários CSS novos

- **`.glass-strong`** — `backdrop-filter: blur(18px)` + borda translúcida; futuro navbar sticky elevado
- **`.bg-hero`** — gradient radial composto com `color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary)/var(--accent), transparent)`; preserva tokens como única fonte de verdade
- **`.bg-gradient-primary`** — gradient linear 135° primary→accent; logo navbar, CTA premium

Todos puro CSS, sem JS, herdam `prefers-reduced-motion` automaticamente (cobertura existente em `globals.css:240-253`).

### Documentação atualizada

- `src/design-system/tokens/colors.ts` — entries `accent` + `accentForeground`
- `docs/design/DESIGN-TOKENS.md` — seção "Wave 6 — Acento narrativo" com tabela, fronteiras de uso (ADR-024 §3) e regra mnemônica
- `docs/architecture/WCAG-AUDIT.md` — seção "Wave 6.0 — `--accent` + utilitários" com valores adotados + output literal `wcag-check.ts`

## 변경 이유

PR #210 (SP-08-1) 에서 legacy GAS UI/Notion live target 통신을 Samhan Public DB/API 로 잠근 후 dev-report 가 명시한 후속 1번 항목 — **DPS 비교 / 품목별 DPS 의 저장내역(history) 탭 복원 + 도메인별 history endpoint** — 을 본 슬라이스(SP-08-2)에서 구현했습니다.

legacy GAS DPS 두 앱(`DPS 입고기록 비교`, `품목별 DPS 입고내역 비교`)은 비교 결과 전체를 gzip+base64 압축해 Notion `저장내역1/2` rich_text 에 chunk 분할 저장하고, 재접속 시 최신 1건 자동 복원 + 기간 조회로 과거 결과 재현하는 동선을 운영자가 사용해 왔습니다. 본 슬라이스는 동일 동선을 우리 service-per-DB(`inventory_db.dps_save_history`) + JSONB payload + 도메인별 4 endpoint 로 이식하고, desktop 두 페이지에 `[실행 | 저장내역]` 2-Tab 을 도입했습니다.

기획서 합의 4건 (Claude PM brainstorming):
1. 범위 = DPS 단독 + 도메인별 history endpoint (공통 `legacy_gas_history` 계층 미도입)
2. Payload = Full JSONB response (legacy parity)
3. 트리거 = 자동 latest upsert + 명시 named append (한 테이블 `save_mode` flag)
4. UI = 2-Tab `[실행 | 저장내역]` (legacy 3-tab 동선과 가장 유사)

## 변경 내용

### Backend (`services/inventory-service`)
- 신규 entity `DpsSaveHistory` (BaseEntity 7 audit + Soft Delete + `JSONB request_params`/`response_payload`).
- enum `DpsProgramType` (`DPS_COMPARE` / `DPS_BY_PRODUCT`), `DpsSaveMode` (`AUTO_LATEST` / `MANUAL_NAMED`).
- Flyway `V11__add_dps_save_history.sql` — partial unique index `WHERE is_deleted=false AND save_mode='AUTO_LATEST'` 로 per (user, programType) AUTO 최신 1건만 활성 (DB 레벨 race guard).
- `DpsSaveHistoryService` — AUTO_LATEST upsert (기존 활성 row soft-delete → 신규 insert + 1회 retry) / MANUAL_NAMED append / payload UTF-8 직렬화 100KB 초과 시 `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` (신규 `ErrorCode` 추가) / 사용자 격리.
- 4 endpoint (`POST` 저장 / `GET` 목록 / `GET /{id}` 상세 / `GET /latest`) — `@PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('WAREHOUSE','MANAGER','MASTER')")` + 한국어 `@Operation`.
- DTO record 4종 (Request / ListRow / DetailResponse / SaveResponse).
- Unit `DpsSaveHistoryServiceTest` + IT `DpsSaveHistoryIT` (Testcontainers PostgreSQL).

### Frontend (`clients/desktop`)
- 신규 component 3개: `DpsHistoryTab.tsx` (저장내역 탭 공통, programType prop) / `DpsRestoredBanner.tsx` (자동 복원 배너) / `DpsSaveDialog.tsx` (topic prompt modal).
- 신규 client `dpsSaveHistoryApi.ts` (4 endpoint, react-query 호환).
- `InventoryDpsComparePage.tsx` + `warehouse/DpsByProductPage.tsx` 모두 2-Tab 도입 + latest 자동 복원 + 저장 / 복원 navigate.
- `mock.ts` 에 DPS history mock 추가 (Vite mock 모드용).

### UUID 비공개 (`feedback_uuid_no_user_visibility.md`)
- `data-testid` 는 row 인덱스 기반 (`dps-history-row-{i}`, `dps-history-row-{i}-created-at`) — UUID 미사용.
- 사용자 노출 라벨 = `topic` / `createdBy(managerName)` / `createdAt` 만.
- Playwright UUID regex scan PASS.

### 산출물
- 기획서: `docs/planning/2026-05-16_sp-08-2-dps-legacy-gas-parity.md` (Claude PM brainstorming, 492 lines).
- dev-report: `docs/dev-reports/sp-08-2-dps-legacy-gas-parity.md`.
- Playwright: `clients/desktop/playwright/sp-08-2-dps-history/sp-08-2-dps-history.spec.ts`.
- QA mock PNG: `docs/qa/sp-08-2-dps-history/screenshots/01~07-*.png` (1280×900).
- QA 스크립트: `scripts/generate-sp-08-2-dps-history-screenshots.ps1`.
- 문서 동기화: `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `clients/desktop/README.md`, `services/inventory-service/README.md`, `migration/decisions/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/handoff/CURRENT-WORK.md`, `docs/dev-reports/sp-08-legacy-gas-db-api-parity.md` (후속 표 1번 행 = `완료 (SP-08-2)`).

## 테스트 방법

| 명령 | 결과 |

| `.\gradlew.bat :services:inventory-service:test --tests "*DpsSaveHistory*" --tests "*DpsCompare*" --tests "*DpsByProduct*" --no-daemon --rerun-tasks` | PASS — XML 집계 36 tests / skipped 0 / failures 0 / errors 0 |

Full rewrite of all 10 chapters. The earlier draft hit the brief but ran
thin as fiction. This pass keeps the premise (IIT Madras friends, Pune
jobs, Hinjewadi, separate first year then live-in) and rebuilds the
story around six leverage moves we discussed:

1. Shameful wants planted in chapter 1, paid off across the book:
   Aditi's quiet relief when Kaustubh's career dips; Kaustubh's need
   for her to need him as her 'Pune guide.'
2. Voice differentiation: Aditi (Nashik, Marathi-medium roots) more
   Devanagari, more direct; Kaustubh (Pune, English-medium FC) more
   code-switching, hedges with humor.
3. One consequential failure: Aditi hides her US onsite offer for six
   weeks. Comes out on the Hinjewadi monsoon-flood night.
4. Three real set pieces replace the summary chapters:
   - Diwali at Aditi's Nashik home (family ambush, grandmother sets
     the engagement clock)
   - Hinjewadi monsoon flood night stranded at his startup office
     (intimacy + the US-offer confrontation)
   - Skipthread layoff day (Aman bhau cuts Anuj and Sneha;
     Kaustubh comes home small)
5. Cut Pranjal, Vikram, and the cousin-Sneha-as-family-spy device.
   Deepen Snehal — the roommate who quietly liked Kaustubh first and
   has to live alongside her best friend dating him.
6. Drop narrator commentary throughout. Less 'this was a brilliant
   reply' explaining the joke; let scenes breathe.

Ends on the mehendi-fading-on-the-palm image instead of the
toothpaste-war listicle. The proposal is replaced by an engagement

# Hypothesis

**Huber loss δ sweep on the triple compound stack: δ ∈ {0.15, 0.5}.**

Your PR #3424 produced a notable side-finding: at clip=0.1, **δ=0.1 (val=74.67) beat δ=0.3 (val=75.11)** even though both regressed against the baseline. That hints that on the current LayerScale+EMA stack, the optimal δ may have shifted from the legacy 0.3 toward something smaller (closer to L1/MAE behavior).

The intuition: LayerScale γ=0.01 already gates residual magnitudes selectively per-channel, and EMA averages out high-frequency parameter noise. Both mechanisms reduce the "heavy-tail residual" pressure that originally motivated δ=0.3 (PR #3213). With those regularizers baked in, a smaller δ (sharper L1 region) might more aggressively reduce the median residual without amplifying outliers (which clip=0.25 already handles).

We bracket δ=0.3 from below (δ=0.15) and above (δ=0.5) at the standard clip=0.25 to find the optimum on the new stack.

## Baseline (target to beat)

- **PR #3192 (LayerScale γ=0.01 + n_freqs=14 + EMA 0.998 + Huber δ=0.3 + clip=0.25)** — current best
- `val_avg/mae_surf_p`: **71.20**
- `test_avg/mae_surf_p`: **62.71**
- Per-split test: single=71.22, rc=72.24, cruise=45.19, re_rand=62.19

## Arms

| Arm | Huber δ | Effect |
|-----|---------|--------|
| arm-1 | 0.15 | Sharper L1 behavior — pushes median residual harder |
| arm-2 | 0.50 | Softer (closer to L2) — uses more quadratic curvature in the loss landscape |

(δ=0.3 is the midpoint and is already validated.)

```bash
cd target && python train.py --epochs 50 \

```

`--huber_delta` already exists. No code changes needed.

body:
The Airlock service generates hundreds of Sentry alerts per hour during routine nsqlookupd outages because `Subscriber.lookupTopic()` uses `>=` to compare the lookup failure count against the threshold, causing every failure after the threshold to log at ERROR level indefinitely. This change switches the comparison to `==` so ERROR is emitted exactly once when the threshold is first reached, with all subsequent failures logged at WARN. The subscriber's resilience behavior is unchanged — it continues retrying and resets the counter on recovery.

## Change Summary

- **`src/main/java/com/sproutsocial/nsq/Subscriber.java`**: Changed the condition at line 203 in `lookupTopic()` from `lookupFailureCount >= this.maxLookupFailuresBeforeError` to `lookupFailureCount == this.maxLookupFailuresBeforeError`. This ensures ERROR is logged only once when the failure count first reaches the threshold (default: 5), and all subsequent consecutive failures continue at WARN level. The failure counter reset on success (line 190) is unchanged, so a new ERROR will still be logged if the host recovers and then fails again.

- **`src/test/java/com/sproutsocial/nsq/SubscriberLookupFailureTest.java`** (new): JUnit 4 unit test that verifies the log level escalation behavior. `errorLoggedExactlyOnceAtThreshold` asserts that across 6 consecutive lookup failures with a threshold of 3, exactly 1 is logged at ERROR (the 3rd) and the remaining 5 at WARN. `errorRelogsAfterRecoveryAndReFailure` verifies that clearing the failure map (simulating recovery) allows a second ERROR to be logged when the threshold is reached again.

- `Document everything ... no exceptions` did not match the codebase,
  which omits docs on test functions, closures, and trivial private
  helpers. Agents over-applied.
- The bullet listing `# Examples` as a default section produced
  synthetic examples on functions nobody calls in isolation -
  `# Examples` actually only appears on the reusable utilities in
  `src/utils/windows.rs`.
- `Minimize inline comments` was correct in spirit but too terse to
  recognise specific anti-patterns, so the rule slid off.

Replace those bullets with a `Documentation and Comments` section that
matches the observed style: full rustdoc with `# Arguments` / `# Returns`
on public items and trait methods, `# Examples` only on reusable
utilities, lighter or omitted docs on private helpers, none on tests
and closures. One good/bad anchor example for docstrings and one for
inline comments, plus pointers to canonical files (`src/utils/windows.rs`,
`src/serde/protocol/mod.rs`, `src/daemon/mod.rs:706-708`,
`src/client/mod.rs:409-411`).

Adds a new `detect gems` command that surfaces hidden-gem tracks by genre and release window across Spotify, SoundCloud, Bandcamp, and Beatport — interactive prompts or flags (`--source/--genre/--count/--date/--no-save`). Beatport queries by exact `genre_id` (real Tech House classification), SoundCloud filters on `playback_count`, Spotify mines editorial playlists by popularity, and Bandcamp uses `discover_web`'s `tag_norm_names` filter (the old endpoint silently ignored genre). Each run is persisted into `detected_tracks` plus two new tables (`gem_scans`, `gem_tracks`), and subsequent runs skip already-found tracks via a release-date-faded exclude set, paging until the requested count of *new* tracks is collected. Also bumps the course_viewer dev script to `vite --host`.
